upper_row_ss: Law and Argument — Transfer Pricing Defense under IRC § 482, Treas. Reg. §§ 1.482-4, 1.482-7, and 1.482-1(d). This section presents the taxpayer's comprehensive legal arguments in support of its transfer pricing positions, including the application of the arm's-length standard, the best method rule, the selection and application of the comparable uncontrolled transaction method for the legacy IP royalty rate, the comparable profits method / transactional net margin method for testing PBI's operating margins, and the income method
lower_row_ss: (Discounted cash flow approach) for the platform contribution transaction valuation. The section addresses the regulatory framework governing qualified cost-sharing arrangements under Treas. Reg. § 1.482-7 and demonstrates that the taxpayer's intercompany pricing is consistent with arm's-length results under each applicable method.

upper_row_ss: Defense of PBI Economic Substance and DEMPE Functions. The Protest presents evidence that PBI possesses genuine economic substance and performs meaningful development, enhancement, maintenance,
lower_row_ss: protection, and exploitation ("DEMPE") functions with respect to the cost-shared intangible property, supporting the allocation of profits to PBI consistent with the arm's-length standard. The defense describes PBI's growth from 52 employees at inception in 2012 to 185 employees by 2020; the conduct of 42 board meetings in Dublin during the examination period; cumulative regulatory expenditures of €47,200,000; PBI's approximately 18,000 square foot office at Sandyford Business Park, Dublin; PBI's independent pricing authority across 68 non-Americas country markets; the role and authority of Managing Director Aidan Naughton; and PBI's independent banking operations with Glenmore Bank Ireland plc.

lower_row_ss: Whitmore Valuation Group LLC — Comparable Profits Method / Transactional Net Margin Method Analysis Report, dated November 2022. This report was prepared by Dr. Helena Vasquez and her team to evaluate the arm's-length nature of PBI's operating margins during Tax Years 2017–2020, applying the CPM under Treas. Reg. § 1.482-5 (the U.S. equivalent of the TNMM under the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines). The analysis tests PBI as the "tested party" by comparing its operating profit margins to those of comparable independent companies performing similar functions, bearing similar risks, and employing similar assets.

upper_row_ss: Revenue Projection Methodology — Americas vs. Non-Americas Splits for Veritaxol, Imvara, and Cerulon. The report describes the methodology used to project PBI's share of future revenues from the exploitation of cost-shared intangible property in non-Americas territories for each of PPC's three principal products: Veritaxol (oncology), Imvara (immunology), and Cerulon (rare disease). The projections are based on product-level
lower_row_ss: market models incorporating therapeutic area market size, expected market share, pricing trends, patent life, regulatory approval timelines, and competitive dynamics. The Americas/non-Americas revenue splits are derived from historical data and market-specific growth assumptions, consistent with the methodology prescribed by Treas. Reg. § 1.482-7(g)(4)(vi).

upper_row_ss: IRS's Income-Method Valuation at $852,000,000 — Identification of Methodological Errors. The report critiques the IRS's alternative PCT valuation of $852,000,000, which was prepared by IRS Economist Dr. Alan Washburne. The report identifies the following methodological errors in the IRS's valuation: (i) application of an inappropriately low WACC of 7.2%, which fails to account for the specific risks of pharmaceutical IP in non-Americas markets (see Tab 9 for detailed WACC analysis); (ii) overstated non-Americas revenue growth projections that are inconsistent with contemporaneous market data and industry forecasts; (iii) an excessively long explicit projection period that extends beyond the useful life of the contributed intangible property; (iv) failure to account for generic competition and patent expiry for key legacy compounds; and (v) use of an inappropriate terminal value methodology that inflates the present value of future cash flows.

upper_row_ss: Critique of IRS's Application of 7.2% WACC — Insufficient Risk Adjustment, Inappropriate Peer Selection. The memorandum demonstrates that the IRS's 7.2% WACC is materially too low because: (i) the IRS used a peer group of large-cap diversified pharmaceutical companies with lower risk profiles than PPC's specialty pharmaceutical portfolio; (ii) the IRS's peer group included companies with significant consumer health and generic drug divisions, which have lower betas and cost of capital than innovative specialty pharma; (iii) the IRS failed to apply a size premium appropriate for PPC's market capitalization; (iv) the IRS failed to make adjustments for the incremental risk of non-Americas market exploitation, including regulatory risk in emerging markets and currency risk; and (v) the
lower_row_ss: IRS's risk-free rate assumption was based on a spot rate rather than a normalized rate consistent with the long-term projection period.

upper_row_ss: Comprehensive Functional Analysis, prepared jointly by Calderwood & Harkness LLP and Whitmore Valuation Group LLC, initially dated October 2022 and revised March 15, 2023. This functional analysis describes the functions performed, assets employed, and risks assumed by PBI during Tax Years 2017 through 2020 in connection with the exploitation of cost-shared and legacy intangible property in non-Americas territories. The analysis was prepared to support PPC's transfer pricing positions and was provided to the IRS
lower_row_ss: examination team in response to Information Document Request No. 12, issued August 10, 2022.

upper_row_ss: PBI's Risks. The functional analysis identifies the principal risks borne by PBI, including: (i) market risk — the risk that non-Americas market revenues will be lower than projected due to competitive dynamics, market access challenges, or changes in clinical practice; (ii) regulatory risk — the risk of delayed or denied regulatory approvals, post-marketing safety findings, or changes in regulatory requirements in non-Americas markets; (iii) pricing risk — the risk of adverse pricing and reimbursement decisions by national health authorities in non-Americas markets; and (iv) currency risk — the risk of adverse changes in foreign exchange rates affecting PBI's revenues and costs, which are denominated in multiple currencies (principally EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, AUD, and various emerging market
lower_row_ss: currencies).

upper_row_ss: IRC § 367(d) — Transfers of Intangibles to Foreign Corporations. Complete text of Internal Revenue Code Section 367(d), which treats certain transfers of intangible property by a U.S. person to a foreign corporation as a sale or exchange of such property in exchange for payments contingent on the productivity, use, or disposition of such property. Section 367(d) is relevant to the characterization and valuation of the platform contribution transaction under the CSA.
lower_row_ss: IRC § 6662(e) — Substantial Valuation Misstatement Penalty (Transfer Pricing). Complete text of Internal Revenue Code Section 6662(e), which imposes a 20% penalty on underpayments of tax attributable to substantial valuation misstatements in connection with transfer pricing transactions. The IRS has asserted this penalty in its NOPA. The taxpayer's defense under Section 6662(e)(3)(B) (reasonable cause and good faith exception based on contemporaneous documentation) is presented in the Formal Protest at Tab 1.8 and 1.9.

upper_row_ss: Treas. Reg. § 1.482-7 — Qualified Cost-Sharing Arrangements. Complete text of Treasury Regulation Section 1.482-7, which governs the tax treatment of qualified cost-sharing arrangements, including the requirements for cost-sharing payments, platform
lower_row_ss: contribution transactions, and the determination of reasonably anticipated benefits. This regulation is the primary regulatory authority governing the PPC-PBI CSA and the PCT valuation at issue.

upper_row_ss: Hollowell & Co. v. Commissioner, T.C. Memo. 2017-25. Analysis of the Amazon decision and its relevance to PPC's cost-sharing, PCT valuation, and economic substance positions. The Amazon case addressed the valuation of a platform contribution transaction in the context of an e-commerce company's cost-sharing
lower_row_ss: arrangement with its Luxembourg subsidiary, and the Tax Court's analysis of the appropriate valuation methods, discount rates, and revenue projections for PCT valuations. The analysis discusses the parallels between the Amazon facts and PPC's PCT valuation, and the implications of the Tax Court's holdings for PPC's defense.

upper_row_ss: GILTI and BEAT Interaction with Proposed § 482 Adjustments. Detailed analysis of the interaction between the IRS's proposed § 482 adjustments and PPC's GILTI and BEAT liabilities for Tax Years 2018, 2019, and 2020. The analysis addresses whether the proposed § 482 adjustments would reduce PPC's GILTI
lower_row_ss: inclusion (by increasing PPC's U.S. taxable income and correspondingly reducing PBI's tested income), and the extent to which any such reduction would offset the tax cost of the proposed adjustments. The analysis also addresses the interaction between the proposed adjustments and PPC's BEAT liability, including whether the adjustments would affect the calculation of the BEAT base erosion percentage and modified taxable income.

upper_row_ss: PPC Corporate Overview. Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. ("PPC") is a Delaware corporation, publicly traded on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol PPCA. PPC's corporate headquarters is located at 2200 Independence Boulevard, Princeton Junction, New Jersey 08550. For fiscal year 2020, PPC reported consolidated revenue of $6.82 billion and consolidated pre-tax income of $1.47 billion. PPC employs approximately 14,500 individuals globally. PPC is a specialty pharmaceutical company focused on the development and commercialization of innovative therapies in the oncology, immunology, and rare disease therapeutic areas. PPC's principal revenue-generating
lower_row_ss: products are Veritaxol (oncology), Imvara (immunology), and Cerulon (rare disease).
